transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-01
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Darin (CSM), Ethan (SE), Lena (Head of Data), Marcus (Platform), Sofia (PM), Tom (Security)
---
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining. just checking audio — can you hear me?
[00:04] Lena: yeah we can hear you, hi maya.
[00:06] Marcus: good afternoon.
[00:10] Maya: awesome. quick agenda: intros, goals for the pilot, data ingestion mapping, network & security, runbook/timeline, then q's and next steps. if anything missing speak up.
[00:20] Sofia: that works, and we want to make sure we cover success criteria — latency and accuracy thresholds.
[00:25] Darin: great. i can take notes on the action items.
[00:30] Maya: perfect. lena, could you start with a quick overview of what you folks are trying to achieve?
[00:36] Lena: sure. so astrawise is rolling out an internal freight-dispatch assistant that pulls from our manifest DB and historical routing logs. main ask is fast routing suggestions (sub-300ms p95 ideally) and embeddings for similarity search across shipments. right now we're prototyping on a small batch job but for pilot need steady production traffic.
[00:55] Marcus: just to add, our infra is aws-only, VPCs in us-west-2, s3 for raw logs, and we run k8s for workloads. we prefer to keep data in our VPC and use either Redwood Dedicated in our account or a private deployment.
[01:12] Ethan: couple quick clarifying q's — when you say "keep data in our VPC" do you mean private deployment OR access via VPC peering into a Redwood-managed VPC?
[01:20] Marcus: good point. initially we want Redwood Dedicated but in our VPC (customer-hosted) if possible. we need to validate egress rules and KMS access.
[01:29] Maya: thanks. for a typical Dedicated flow we support both: dedicated capacity in our cloud with private networking or we can deploy private control plane in your account. both options have tradeoffs on maintenance and speed to spin up.
[01:42] Tom: quick security callout — we have to stay SOC2-aligned and our infosec team requires KMS/HSM control, audit logs for token usage, and SAML SSO enforced. also retention rules for raw logs (90 days) and RL for embeddings — can you support that?
[02:01] Darin: yes, we have runbooks for KMS integration and audit log retention. we'll share the security checklist after this call.
[02:08] Tom: okay. also curious about on-prem option later — we might go air-gapped for certain clients.
[02:14] Maya: understood — we have an on-prem/offline path but it adds project lead time and a different support SLA. we'll include that in the doc.
[02:21] [short pause, typing]
[02:35] Maya: moving to ingestion — lena, what does the data shape look like? fields, sequence length, sizes?
[02:41] Lena: manifest entries are ~1.5k chars avg, routing logs vary but typical prompt plus context <2k tokens; we also plan to store embeddings for 18M shipments eventually but pilot will be ~100k vectors.
[02:56] Ethan: ok that's helpful. pilot numbers are moderate; for 100k vectors typical embedding cost and throughput are manageable with quantized models. question: are you planning real-time calls at 100 rps or batched lookup?
[03:10] Sofia: we aim for near-real-time — around 50 to 100 rps at peak for the assistant, plus background batch builds for nightly reindex.
[03:19] Ethan: so we should plan caching + prefix KV — sorry K-V cache — to reduce token regen and keep latency SLOs, especially for repeated contexts. we can show recommended batching settings in the optimize playbook.
[03:32] Marcus: do you have recommended model variants? we prefer open models but with high perf.
[03:36] Maya: yes, we'll propose 2 variants: a lower-cost quantized 8-bit variant for embeddings/less critical generation and a higher fidelity variant for complex routing reasoning. we'll include throughput benchmarks from similar workloads.
[03:50] Marcus: great. any special infra constraints like GPU types?
[03:53] Ethan: if you're running customer-hosted, we recommend A10s or H100s depending on latency vs cost. for pilot, a small A10 pool is usually sufficient.
[04:02] Tom: about KMS — do we need to share keys with Redwood? our policy prefers customer-managed keys.
[04:08] Maya: we support CMKs (customer-managed keys) via AWS KMS. Redwood doesn't keep the unwrapped keys; we integrate using IAM roles and a KMS policy. i'll send the exact IAM role template.
[04:17] Tom: got it. and audit logs — can you ship token-level logs to our s3?
[04:22] Darin: yes, we can forward structured audit logs to your s3 or a logging endpoint; retention policy is configurable.
[04:28] Lena: one more data question — embeddings storage. do you recommend using Redwood's managed vector store or our own?
[04:35] Ethan: for pilot we suggest using customer-managed vector store (e.g., opensearch or Pinecone) to validate retrieval latencies and then optionally shift to Redwood-managed cache for lower read costs. we'll outline both in the runbook.
[04:48] [05:00 marker missing - short cross talk]
[05:10] Maya: timeline: propose two-week pilot prep (network + access), then a four-week pilot with perf tests in week 2 and 4. does that align with your timelines?
[05:22] Sofia: yes, we want pilot live by mid-july if possible.
[05:25] Marcus: mid-july ok, we have infra windows to schedule.
[05:28] Maya: great. i'll put a tentative calendar.
[05:35] [06:00] Marcus: about firewall whitelists — what's the minimum set you need?
[05:40] Ethan: we'll provide CIDR blocks and FQDNs, plus a recommended egress port list. also, if you prefer a VPC peering approach we can work with that.
[05:50] Tom: any data-in-transit encryption specifics?
[05:53] Maya: TLS1.3 standard. mutual TLS for private deployments is supported if you want mTLS for in-cluster comms.
[06:00] [06:15] Lena: okay. on success criteria — we'd measure: p95 latency < 300ms for 90% of calls, routing accuracy uplift >10% over baseline, embedding nearest-neighbor recall >85% on our test set.
[06:30] Darin: noted. we'll capture those as pilot KPIs.
[06:34] [07:00] Sofia: thinking about rollback — if the model starts to drift, can we auto-fallback to a simpler model?
[07:05] Ethan: yes, Redwood supports rollout policies and automatic fallback to pinned model variants. we can configure canary ratios and automatic rollback on regression alerts.
[07:15] Maya: we'll include an eval harness for your prompt suites so you get regression alerts.
[07:20] [07:45] Tom: procurement question — what license terms for Dedicated in-customer account vs Redwood-hosted?
[07:28] Maya: Dedication in your account is a platform fee + per-instance cost; hosted Dedicated reduces maintenance but we can share a comparison sheet. i'll loop in sales for the formal quote.
[07:40] [08:00] Marcus: one operational q — how do we do model updates? are rollouts manual?
[08:03] Ethan: rollouts can be automated with staged canaries; you can pin model versions per route. we also keep model version history and traces for each request.
[08:13] Lena: any known issues with token accounting? we need precise per-team cost attribution.
[08:18] Darin: we expose token-level costing and per-route breakdowns in the console. we'll set up a cost-view for your team as part of pilot.
[08:26] [09:00] [brief tangent about billing metrics — some cross talk]
[09:20] Maya: security deep-dive — tom what are your blockers?
[09:25] Tom: primarily KMS control, SAML attributes mapping, audit evidence for SOC2, and encrypted at-rest for embeddings. also we need to ensure no PII is persisted in logs — can you redact?
[09:36] Ethan: we have configurable filters to mask or omit fields from logs; also configurable retention. for embeddings we can optionally store encrypted blobs with your KMS.
[09:48] Tom: good. also need MFA and SCIM provisioning for SSO.
[09:52] Darin: we support SAML SSO + SCIM for user provisioning. we'll attach the SSO guide.
[09:58] [10:15] Maya: okay, let's capture the pilot success criteria again and owners.
[10:20] Darin: action item recap: maya to send runbook/deck; ethan to propose perf test windows; marcus to confirm network; tom to send security Q's; lena to share sample payloads.
[10:35] Lena: noted. i'll get the sample S3 paths and a small subset of manifests for ingestion tests.
[10:40] Sofia: we also need an initial dataset for the eval harness — lena will pick ~500 examples.
[10:45] Marcus: about perf test sim — we run a traffic generator in k8s, do you need any client certs?
[10:50] Ethan: if you're using VPC peering, no client certs needed; if private deployment with mTLS we'll coordinate cert exchange.
[10:58] [12:00] Maya: risks: on-prem timeline, KMS policy approvals, and model quality regressions. we'll call those out in the risk register.
[12:08] Tom: sounds good. minor ask — can we get SLA on latency for the pilot? at least an internal target.
[12:14] Maya: yes we'll provide target SLOs in the runbook and note what we can commit to in Dedicated vs private.
[12:20] [13:00] [quick pause]
[13:10] Darin: scheduling — i'll send a 30-min weekly cadence, first check-in 2026-06-09.
[13:20] Maya: any other q's from astrawise?
[13:24] Sofia: none from me.
[13:26] Lena: just one: who will be our primary support contact?
[13:31] Darin: i'll be CSM lead; maya AE; ethan SE for technical deep dives.
[13:36] [14:00] Marcus: ok thanks everyone.
[13:40] Maya: thanks, we'll follow up with the runbook and security checklist.
[14:00] [call ends]
